subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — Acme Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: POC next steps & workload intake (Acme Health)

Hi Jason —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the POC/trial: 

Summary of needs (as I captured them)
- Primary use case: patient triage assistant in the Acme Health clinician portal (summarization + structured triage suggestions).
- Success criteria (proposed): latency <= 350ms p50 for a 512-token response, throughput to support 80 RPS steady-state per region, and model quality matching current baseline in your internal eval set (we'll ask for a small eval set).
- Data scope: only de-identified patient notes for POC; no PHI in model input for trial.

POC plan / ask from your team
1) Workload & traffic profile: RPS, typical request/response token lengths, concurrency, burst patterns, and any time-of-day peaks.
2) Evaluation plan & success criteria: a short list of sample prompts and the acceptance thresholds (F1/precision/recall or qualitative pass/fail).
3) Timeline & owners: proposed pilot start date, who will be the day-to-day contact on your side for infra/tests, and procurement steps if needed.

I've attached a one-page intake spreadsheet to capture the workload profile and evaluation artifacts — could you and Priya fill the workload/traffic tab and drop your sample evals in the Drive link?

Next steps
- Can you return the intake by Tue 20 Apr?
- If agreeable, we can schedule a 30-min technical kickoff Wednesday 21 Apr with our infra engineer (Dylan) to go over latency targets and any integration points.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acmehealth-poc-intake.xlsx (workload + eval template)

From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: Re: POC next steps & workload intake (Acme Health)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Priya and I discussed and we populated the intake sheet with initial numbers (see attached traffic sample). High level answers below: 

Workload / traffic profile (initial)
- Steady-state RPS: ~80 RPS across our primary region (us-west), with a target 95th percentile concurrency of ~120.
- Typical request size (tokens):  input ~40-120 tokens (short notes + metadata), response ~200-600 tokens (summaries + structured suggestions).
- Burst patterns: morning check-in windows (08:00–10:00 local) cause bursts up to 300 RPS for ~5–10 mins; end-of-day activities around 17:00 see smaller spikes (~150 RPS).
- Expected total API calls during 2-week POC: ~95k calls.

Evaluation artifacts
- We can provide a 200-item de-identified eval set (CSV) with expected labels (triage category + key-findings).
- Primary quality signal: category F1 >= 0.78 and clinician accept-rate > 85% (qualitative review).

Timeline & owners
- We can return the completed intake today.
- Proposed POC window: 26 Apr — 10 May (2 weeks).
- Day-to-day contacts: Priya Desai (prod owner) and myself. Priya will own test execution; I will own procurement/legal coordination.

I'll attach the traffic sample (acmehealth-traffic-sample.csv) and the intake we filled. Let us know if you want any of these as a Drive folder instead.

—Jason
Jason Lee
Head of Product, Acme Health
jason.lee@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: POC next steps & workload intake (Acme Health)

Jason — great, this is exactly what we needed, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups and confirmation of our plan: 

1) Intake received — thanks for the CSV and the numbers. We'll run a quick capacity/readiness check against the profile you provided. Dylan will kick off a perf run to validate latency at the 80 RPS steady-state and the burst patterns you listed.

2) Technical kickoff
- Proposed: Wed 21 Apr, 10:00am PT / 13:00pm ET, 30 min. Attendees: Dylan (infra), Marissa (solutions), Priya (you), Jason (you) + Ben. Please confirm.

3) Success criteria validation
- We'll ingest your 200-item eval set into our eval harness and run the candidate model(s) agreed during the call (we suggested Llama-3-70B-quant and a 13B quant variant for cost/latency tradeoffs).
- We'll report: p50/p95 latency for request/response lengths you shared, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and the quality metrics (F1/clinician accept-rate).

4) Ownership & follow-ups
- Redwood owner: Ben (deal), Marissa (solutions lead), Dylan (infra).
- Acme owners: Priya (day-to-day), Jason (sponsor/procurement).

5) Timeline
- Intake done: 19 Apr (complete)
- Tech kickoff: 21 Apr (pending confirmation)
- POC window: 26 Apr — 10 May
- Deliverables by end of POC: perf summary, cost estimate for production scale, and a 1-page quality report.

If that all looks good I'll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and a short pre-kickoff checklist for the infra team (SSH keys, allowed IPs, dataset upload link).

Thanks — looking forward to Wednesday.

Best,
Ben

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: POC next steps & workload intake (Acme Health)

Ben / Jason —

Confirming the kickoff time works for us. I will be the primary point for test execution and will upload the de-identified eval CSV to the Drive folder you shared this afternoon.

A couple quick notes from my side:
- For security we will need to whitelist the Redwood dedicated IP ranges; I'll share the list with Dylan during the kickoff.
- We prefer the 13B quant variant for the initial run (cost sensitivity), and if that looks good we'll iterate to the 70B for quality checks.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Product Manager, Acme Health
priya.desai@acmehealth.com
+1 (650) 555-0199
